Why citation match is insufficient
Citation is an important legal signal, but it is not

plex issues such as retroactivity, transition clauses,
tolling, and multi-rule statutory interpretation are

is intentional because it yields a controlled setting

application can be diagnosed cleanly.

the benchmark useful for measuring whether re-

AuthorityFirst-RAG: A Diagnostic
Retriever
4.1
Method overview
AuthorityFirst-RAG is a transparent authority-first
retrieval procedure. We do not present it as a univer-
sal neural retriever or as a deployable legal search
engine. Instead, it is designed to test which legal-
structural signals matter for law-in-force retrieval.
The pipeline first extracts query structure, then iden-
tifies candidate authorities, applies temporal scop-
ing, retrieves within the candidate authority scope,
and finally ranks passages by rule-support signals.
AuthorityFirst-RAG is implemented with deter-
ministic rule-based parsing and heuristic feature-
based ranking rather than a learned retriever. Ci-
tation cues, operative dates, fact values, units, and
comparator signals are extracted using regular ex-
pressions and rule-based normalization. After tem-
poral filtering, ranking combines authority/citation
match, BM25 relevance, lexical overlap, thresh-
old/unit compatibility, and comparator cues; no
learned parameters are used.

Discussion
7.1
Law in force is different from semantic
relevance
A relevant passage is not necessarily legally appli-
cable. Semantic and citation-aware retrieval reward
topical and authority-like signals; law-in-force re-
trieval adds validity and rule support. Wrong ver-
sions are hard because they often share section
numbers, headings, definitions, and most wording;
in LawInForce-eCFR, the decisive difference may
be a single threshold or deadline.
7.2
Wrong versions have near-zero utility
Wrong versions can be more harmful than irrel-
evant text because they appear authoritative and
answer-bearing. This is why Recall@1 matters: if
the first passage is the wrong version, the system
may rely on authority that cannot govern the facts.
7.3
The dual bottleneck
AuthorityFirst-RAG improves top-rank retrieval,
but downstream answer gains remain modest. Ver-
sioned legal RAG therefore has a dual bottleneck:
selecting the law in force and applying its numeric
rule. Better evidence shifts failures from semantic
grounding toward rule application, showing that
retrieval and rule application are distinct failure
modes. Controlled numeric amendments make this
split diagnosable because old/new versions, fact
values, answer flips, and gold evidence are verifi-
able.

7.1 Law in force is different from semantic
relevance
A relevant passage is not necessarily legally appli-
cable. Semantic and citation-aware retrieval reward
topical and authority-like signals; law-in-force re-

sions are hard because they often share section

be a single threshold or deadline.

Wrong versions can be more harmful than irrel-

answer-bearing. This is why Recall@1 matters: if
the first passage is the wrong version, the system
may rely on authority that cannot govern the facts.

AuthorityFirst-RAG improves top-rank retrieval,
but downstream answer gains remain modest. Ver-
sioned legal RAG therefore has a dual bottleneck:
selecting the law in force and applying its numeric
rule. Better evidence shifts failures from semantic
grounding toward rule application, showing that
retrieval and rule application are distinct failure
modes. Controlled numeric amendments make this
split diagnosable because old/new versions, fact
values, answer flips, and gold evidence are verifi-
able.

Conclusion
We introduced LawInForce-eCFR, a diagnostic
benchmark for law-in-force retrieval in versioned
legal RAG, together with AuthorityFirst-RAG, a
transparent retriever for authority, temporal valid-

topically relevant or citation-matched law can still
be legally wrong when it is not in force.
The results show a dual bottleneck: retrieve
applicable authority, then apply its numeric rule.

misapply thresholds, deadlines, or comparator di-
rection. Versioned legal RAG must therefore be
both applicability-aware and rule-faithful.

Limitations
LawInForce-eCFR covers U.S. federal eCFR/CFR
regulations and focuses on clean numeric thresh-
old amendments. It does not cover other jurisdic-
tions, statutes, case law, contracts, agency guid-
ance, or legal sources with different versioning
practices. The benchmark also excludes transi-
tion clauses, retroactivity, tolling, cross-references,
multi-condition rules, exceptions, and difficult le-
gal interpretation.
Numeric thresholds, deadlines, caps, percent-
ages, counts, penalties, ages, and frequencies are
useful for controlled diagnosis because they sup-
port deterministic answer flips across versions.
Many legal questions, however, require broader
doctrinal reasoning, distributed definitions, factual
uncertainty, agency discretion, and multi-step statu-
tory interpretation. The results should therefore
be interpreted as evidence about a controlled law-
in-force retrieval failure mode, not as a complete
evaluation of legal reasoning or legal advice.
AuthorityFirst-RAG is a transparent diagnostic
retriever, not a deployable legal search engine. It
assumes structured citation, section, paragraph, and
validity-interval metadata, and metadata-assisted
baselines should be interpreted diagnostically. De-
ployed systems may require more robust citation
normalization, version alignment, and authority res-
